rationale: The diagnosis is legitimate — the archived RolloverGap quotient had an unstable/sign-flipping denominator, and re-expressing the same shortfall over a strictly positive scale is a defensible fix rather than a cosmetic tweak — but it is a re-specification of an already-tested economic quantity, is a single-theme ratio rather than a genuine cross-theme interaction, and sits close to standard short-term-debt-coverage components of published distress scores, so the upside is a cleaner estimate of a known effect.

This is the fifth MIN-structure variant in the archive and merely swaps che/lct for another funding-capacity leg that itself contains gross profit in the numerator, making it mechanically and economically near-collinear with WeakestLinkSolvency (both legs share revt−cogs), so any improvement will be hard to attribute to a new mechanism rather than leg-scaling noise.

The stated purpose is a placebo/diagnostic that the authors expect to be *weaker*, which contradicts the declared positive EXPECTED_SIGN and means it is not a candidate signal at all; moreover, because RANK is non-negative, the expression is by construction a reweighted Novy-Marx gross-profitability sort — a direct rediscovery of a published anomaly — and the identification question could be answered more cleanly by simply regressing the parent signal on gross profitability.

Gross profitability is highly persistent, so its five-year TS_MIN is nearly a monotone transform of its current level, making this a high-correlation restatement of WeakestLinkSolvency (the archive's best signal) combined with the already-tested floor concept from DemonstratedCoverageFloor, and the proposal offers no evidence that the floor and level legs are actually distinct.

This is the first use of oancf, and the signed conversion-gap leg is genuinely orthogonal to a profitability level sort, though the reviewer should be aware that z(OCF/at) − z(GP/at) is close to a scaled accruals measure and thus partially rediscovers Sloan/Ball et al. cash-based profitability — the novelty rests entirely on the liquidity-stress conditioning, which must be shown to add over the unconditional accrual leg.

Replacing the failed volatility leg with a capacity-adjusted profit level is a defensible response to the archive's evidence that second-moment quality channels are weak, but because RANK(NEG(wcap/at)) is non-negative this again reduces largely to an intensity-weighted profitability sort, so the design should be checked against a plain (revt−cogs−dp)/at benchmark to show the working-capital conditioning contributes anything.
